narrative_purpose: Shows why the moon's interior never cools: the gas giant filling the sky, and a cutaway of the moon's own interior glowing with frictional heat along its internal boundaries — the heat source that keeps vent fields running for billions of years.
subject: An enormous banded gas giant occupying most of the upper frame, its cloud bands broad and softly striped, a thin ring system crossing in front of it edge-on. Below and in front of it sits the curved limb of a moon, cut away like a sliced fruit to reveal concentric interior layers: a thin dark crust, a thick mantle layer, and a small dense core. Along the boundaries between those layers, and along a set of internal stress lines running through the mantle, the rock glows faintly warm as though heated from friction. The moon's cut face is slightly deformed into an oval rather than a perfect circle, stretched along the direction of the gas giant.
scene: Space above the moon's night side, the gas giant dominating the sky, a scatter of faint stars in the small remaining dark gaps.
camera: A wide view from a vantage well off the moon's surface, the gas giant high in frame and the cutaway moon limb curving across the lower portion.
light: Cool dim reflected light from the gas giant washing the moon's outer surface; the interior lit entirely by its own faint warm amber glow concentrated at the layer boundaries and stress lines, fading into the dark rock between them.
palette: Deep void-indigo space, the gas giant in muted teal and stone-grey bands, the moon's rock layers in deep teal-indigo and desaturated stone, warm ember-amber restricted to the internal heated boundaries as the scarce accent.
style: Painterly astronomical plate crossed with a geological cutaway, hand-painted banding on the gas giant, textured rather than rendered.
detail_level: Soft broad detail on the gas giant's cloud bands, crisp on the moon's cut interior layers and glowing stress lines, stars kept faint and sparse.
composition: Gas giant filling the upper two thirds with its limb curving across, the cutaway moon in the lower left, a dark uncluttered region of space at the right for an overlaid callout.
consistency_notes: The gas giant must read as a real observed body with soft painted cloud bands, not a poster planet with high saturation. The moon's deformation should be subtle — noticeably oval, not dramatically squashed. Warm glow confined to the interior only; the surface stays cool-lit.
